summary: Eight connected Daxia/Fuhan source-context repairs: retain existing AD346 one-sided bounds and make their narrative basis explicit. Partial uninstalled proposal; no date approval.

before.event: Ma Qiu took Daxia; the protector seized grand administrator Song Yan and opened the city.
before.unresolvedReason: No new era year is given after 永和二年. A closed later Yonghe year is not in the Chinese.

sourceDate.text: 梁式執太守宋晏，以城應秋; 秋遣晏以書 (s0531–s0532, following Chonghua’s 永和二年 accession in s0499)

after.event: Ma Qiu took Daxia; the protector seized grand administrator Song Yan and opened the city.

changes.reason: s0531 identifies Song Yan as the grand administrator seized by Liang Shi when Ma Qiu takes Daxia, and s0532 has Ma Qiu use Yan’s letter. 季龍又令麻秋 resumes the same named invader from s0504 in Chonghua’s reign introduced at s0499. These are Song Yan’s own contemporary capture and coerced correspondence, not an ancient exemplum. The existing onOrAfter AD346 floor is supported by that accession and connected campaign sequence; no exact capture year or upper endpoint is supplied.

before.event: Ma Qiu used Song Yan’s letter to lure garrison commandant Song Ju, who refused to live basely.
before.unresolvedReason: No new era year is given after 永和二年. A closed later Yonghe year is not in the Chinese.

sourceDate.text: 秋遣晏以書誘宛戍都尉宋矩 (s0532–s0535, following the renewed Daxia attack under Chonghua after s0499)

after.event: Ma Qiu used Song Yan’s letter to lure garrison commandant Song Ju, who refused to live basely.

changes.reason: s0532 explicitly addresses the letter to Song Ju, and s0533–s0535 give Ju’s refusal to accept dishonorable survival. This is the immediate consequence of Ma Qiu’s renewed Daxia capture in s0531 after Chonghua’s s0499 accession, not a detached biographical flashback. Preserve Ju’s refusal and the existing onOrAfter AD346 bound. Neither his speech nor the narrative states a closed event year or a latest possible date.

before.event: Lang Tan, grand administrator of Jinyang, wanted to abandon Fuhan’s outer wall and later let Ma Qiu’s men onto the northwest corner.
before.unresolvedReason: No new era year is given after 永和二年. A closed later Yonghe year is not in the Chinese.

sourceDate.text: 俄而麻秋進攻枹罕; 郎坦…教軍士李嘉 (s0544–s0550, sequel to Chonghua’s accession and current campaign)

after.event: Lang Tan, grand administrator of Jinyang, wanted to abandon Fuhan’s outer wall and later let Ma Qiu’s men onto the northwest corner.

changes.reason: s0544 introduces the Fuhan siege with 俄而 after Chonghua’s decision 重華從之 in s0543 and the same-month rites discussion beginning s0537. Lang Tan first argues to abandon the outer wall, then s0550 explicitly connects his discontent 言之不從 to admitting the enemy. This connected action belongs to the reign established in s0499; the existing onOrAfter AD346 lower bound is warranted. 是月 and 俄而 do not identify a numbered year, so no exact year, month conversion, or upper endpoint is introduced.

before.event: Grand administrator of Wucheng Zhang Quan said abandoning the outer wall would lose the great task.
before.unresolvedReason: No new era year is given after 永和二年. A closed later Yonghe year is not in the Chinese.

sourceDate.text: 武城太守張悛曰…棄外城則大事去矣 (s0545 during the Fuhan siege following Chonghua’s s0499 accession)

after.event: Grand administrator of Wucheng Zhang Quan said abandoning the outer wall would lose the great task.

changes.reason: Zhang Quan’s warning in s0545 directly answers Lang Tan’s proposal in s0544 during Ma Qiu’s 俄而 advance on Fuhan. s0546 says Zhang Qu followed that advice, fixing this as the current defence rather than quoted historical counsel. The campaign is in Chonghua’s reign after his s0499 accession. Its existing onOrAfter AD346 floor accurately expresses the chronology; the source supplies neither Quan’s exact speaking year nor an upper endpoint.

before.event: Colonel Zhang Qu held Fuhan’s great city, drove back the breach, and executed Li Jia.
before.unresolvedReason: No new era year is given after 永和二年. A closed later Yonghe year is not in the Chinese.

sourceDate.text: 張璩…固守大城…璩戮李嘉以徇 (s0546–s0552, Fuhan defence in the post-s0499 accession campaign)

after.event: Colonel Zhang Qu held Fuhan’s great city, drove back the breach, and executed Li Jia.

changes.reason: s0546 names Zhang Qu as the defender who accepts Zhang Quan’s advice. After Lang Tan’s collusion in s0550, s0551 has Qu dispatch the named defenders to repel the breach and s0552 has him execute Li Jia. The repeated 璩 and causal sequence establish one current siege after Chonghua’s accession at s0499. Preserve the existing onOrAfter AD346 bound, the actions and owner; neither the execution nor defence is individually assigned a calendar year or upper endpoint.

before.event: Jilong again ordered Ma Qiu to advance and capture Daxia.
before.unresolvedReason: s0531 季龍又令麻秋 has no new era year after 永和二年.

sourceDate.text: 季龍又令麻秋進陷大夏 (s0531; renewed order in the campaign after Chonghua’s 永和二年 accession in s0499)

after.event: Jilong again ordered Ma Qiu to advance and capture Daxia.

changes.reason: s0503 has Chonghua send a memorial to Shi Jilong, and s0504 has Jilong send Ma Qiu and others to invade. s0531 季龍又令麻秋 is an explicitly renewed order by the same ruler in that war narrative. The event therefore belongs to Jilong’s own dispatch activity after Chonghua’s s0499 accession, supporting the existing onOrAfter AD346 lower bound. No lifespan endpoint, exact later Yonghe year, or retrospective death notice is used.

before.unresolvedReason: The death is stated in the cited Chinese and follows the 永和二年 cluster with no new era year. Use the same onOrAfter 346 bound as the host narrative; do not import an external later year.
before.event: Song Ju first killed his wife and children, then cut his own throat and died.

sourceDate.text: 於是先殺妻子，自刎而死 (s0536, directly following Song Ju’s refusal in the post-s0499 Daxia campaign)

after.event: Song Ju first killed his wife and children, then cut his own throat and died.

changes.reason: s0532–s0535 identify Song Ju as the commander refusing Ma Qiu’s inducement. s0536 於是 makes his killing of his family and suicide the immediate outcome of that refusal, not another person’s death or a retrospective allusion. The linked Daxia attack in s0531 is a renewal of the current invasion after Chonghua’s accession at s0499. The existing onOrAfter AD346 death bound is supported; the actual death year and an upper endpoint remain unstated.

before.event: Zhang Qu executed Li Jia as a warning after the wall breach.

sourceDate.text: 璩戮李嘉以徇 (s0552 following Li Jia’s collusion in the post-s0499 Fuhan campaign)

after.event: Zhang Qu executed Li Jia as a warning after the wall breach.

changes.reason: s0550 names Li Jia as the soldier instructed by Lang Tan to contact Ma Qiu and bring enemy soldiers onto Fuhan’s wall. s0551 repels that breach, and s0552 explicitly says Zhang Qu executed Li Jia as a warning. The named victim and immediate military sequence establish Li Jia’s death in the campaign after Chonghua’s s0499 accession. Retain only its existing onOrAfter AD346 lower bound; no exact execution year, external death date, or upper endpoint is inferred.
